clue.text: Craftsman who has an inflationary effect on his products

definitions.text: Craftsman who has an inflationary effect on his products

parts.words: Craftsman who has an inflationary effect on his products
parts.note: the maker literally inflates his wares with his breath, the inflation being air rather than prices

explanation.surface: An economist's jibe at a maker whose goods keep pushing prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflationary' points to economics, but the inflating here is done with breath through a pipe into molten material.
explanation.definitionFit: This artisan shapes molten silica by puffing air into it through a long tube.

clue.text: Range could be put down in noughts

indicators.note: letters put down afresh, written in another arrangement, signal an anagram

explanation.surface: A scorer notes that the range can be recorded in zeros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be put down' rearranges NOUGHTS; 'in' is a link. The definition is the distance a gun can reach, as in 'within gunshot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance a fired bullet can carry is its reach, as in 'out of gunshot'.

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's report card.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner is from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A single year's entry in a chronicle of events is a historical record.

clue.text: Drink now mixed in separate container

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the separating word
container marks the separating word as the one holding the rest

parts.note: sunder means split apart, separate

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of now are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink is mixed now and poured into a separate glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns NOW into DOWN, and 'in ... container' puts that inside SUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening alcoholic drink taken at sunset, a colonial term.

indicators.note: in a down clue the number sits on top of the benefit

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
aid is help or benefit

explanation.surface: Someone put a figure on a welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts L above AID.
explanation.definitionFit: Put down or set in position, as one sets a table.

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A worn-out hippy roaming far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'far-out' hides the split: 'out' rearranges WEARY FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone journeying on foot is a wanderer on the road.

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduation party with dancing and drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom step of African origin.

clue.text: Possibly respect a sign of authority

indicators.note: possibly says the word respect could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Respect could be a mark of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod a monarch carries is an emblem of royal power.

indicators.note: repeatedly means the rearranged word is given twice
out signals the letters of four are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Four people go out, their clothes rustling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns FOUR into FROU, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The swishing sound of silk skirts as their wearer moves.

clue.text: Ninety-ton order, yet one of no account

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order signals an anagram of the words before

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that the man who ordered ninety tons is a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges the nine letters of NINETY-TON; 'yet' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance or standing is a nobody, a cipher.

clue.text: Means of communication for a TV detective

explanation.surface: A television sleuth is said to have his own way of sending messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot-and-dash telegraph code bears this name, as does Colin Dexter's Oxford inspector of a long-running ITV series.

explanation.surface: Someone stayed put and kept a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both stayed or lingered and kept gripping something tightly.

clue.text: Missile launcher fitted to aircraft carriers

explanation.surface: A description of launching gear installed on warships.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the boy's forked sling; the second is the steam device that flings planes off a flight deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling or siege engine hurls missiles, and the same name is given to the deck device that launches planes from carriers.

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
money advanced is money lent

explanation.surface: Saying thanks when someone gives you a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is a link here. The definition is an ancient unit of money: a weight of silver or gold in Greece and Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In antiquity this was a sum of currency, a large weight of precious metal, as in the biblical parable.

clue.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

definitions.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

parts.words: Women who saw wartime service in the field
parts.note: in the field is literal, farm work, rather than the military sense of the front line

explanation.surface: A tribute to women who served on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Land Army sent British women to work on farms in both World Wars; 'in the field' means on farmland, not in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: The British wartime organisation placed women in agricultural jobs while men fought.

parts.note: stock is read as ancestry or breeding rather than shop goods, and a good line is a fine lineage

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper asking whether a popular product is available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line in stock' suggests merchandise on shelves, but stock means bloodline and line means descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorded ancestry, especially a distinguished one for an animal, is a fine line of descent.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests or amusing might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A person who is either silly or entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the nine letters of OR AMUSING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant or stupid person, a dunce.

parts.note: addresses are read as talks delivered to an audience, not postal addresses

explanation.surface: Labels for parcels that need posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Addresses' and 'delivery' suggest the post, but a speaker delivers addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal talks given to audiences are orations delivered from a platform.

clue.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

definitions.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

parts.words: He suffers from a lack of balance
parts.note: balance is read as money in an account rather than physical steadiness

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps falling over because of a poor sense of balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balance' sounds like equilibrium, but it is a bank balance that is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone declared insolvent by a court cannot pay his debts.

clue.text: It helps a tramp to settle down

definitions.text: It helps a tramp to settle down

parts.words: It helps a tramp to settle down
parts.note: a tramp is a cargo ship without fixed route, and settling down means sitting steady and low in the water

explanation.surface: Something that helps a vagrant find a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' suggests a homeless wanderer, but a tramp steamer is a cargo ship; weight in its hold keeps it stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy material carried low in a ship's hold steadies it.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of lunge are knocked out of order

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for strongly or loudly

explanation.surface: A fencer lunges hard and overpowers the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LUNGE into ENGUL; F, the music abbreviation for forte, is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow up or submerge completely, as a flood or a feeling might.

clue.text: It makes sense if it is used to win at cards

definitions.text: it is used to win at cards

indicators.note: makes means the answer's letters can be rearranged to form the words sense if

explanation.surface: A card player's skill explained as what turns a hand to sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes sense if' reads the other way round: the answer rearranged makes SENSE IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge play trying to take a trick with a lower card while a higher one is out.

clue.text: Having had a rise, a man goes on holiday

indicators.note: goes on means the man's name is placed after the holiday word

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: After a pay rise, a fellow takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having had a rise' suggests a pay rise, but it is bread that has risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough treated with yeast has risen before baking.

parts.note: end means last, the final part
or offers a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: Wondering where a witch would finally choose to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's Witch of Endor was consulted by King Saul; the place was her home.
explanation.definitionFit: This biblical town was home to the medium Saul consulted before his last battle.

clue.text: Where you must go if you get time

definitions.text: Where you must go if you get time

parts.words: Where you must go if you get time
parts.note: time is read as a ... sentence rather than spare time

explanation.surface: Advice on how to spend any free hours you have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get time' sounds like having leisure, but 'doing time' is serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is where convicts serve their sentences.

indicators.note: straggling means the letters of curbs spread out of order

explanation.surface: Restraints on untidy, sprawling shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with stunted trees and shrubs is low growth or brushwood.

clue.text: A voice raised in triumphal tones

indicators.note: raised in means brought up inside, so the voice is held within the words triumphal tones

explanation.surface: A singer lifts his voice in a victory song.
explanation.walkthrough: The voice sits inside 'triumphAL TOnes'; 'raised' also hints at a high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female or highest adult male singing part.

indicators.note: out here means the help word sits outside, around me

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone instructed me to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says AID goes on the outside of ME; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed or steered towards a target, as a shot or a remark is aimed.

parts.note: a hall is an entrance passage or corridor
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Paying fares in Germany comes with assurances.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamps assayers put on gold and silver certify its purity, hence marks of quality generally.

explanation.surface: Someone reliable who nonetheless did the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means reliable and dependable, and also to blame for something, as in 'who is to blame?'
